description: An obligation that regulated actors must discharge by proof. Published by the regulator. The `statement` field is compilable source in the theory's DSL, not a paraphrase of one — there is no second, informal version of the rule that could drift from the formal one.

citation.description: Where this obligation comes from in law, e.g. 'Fair Districting Act § 2'.

theory.description: Pinned by CID, so amending the theory cannot silently change what an existing requirement means.

artifactType.description: Which collection this quantifies over. Must appear in the theory's artifactTypes.

statement.description: The requirement as written, in the theory's DSL. This exact text appears in the theory package and elaborates to `leanProp`; the checker does not re-parse it.

leanProp.description: Fully-qualified name of the predicate the statement elaborates to, e.g. 'Redistrict.FairDistrictingAct.section2'. The checker applies this to the decoded artifact to synthesize the proof obligation.

clauses.description: Names of the conjuncts, in order. Lets a refutation say which part of the rule was violated instead of only that the rule was violated.

supersedes.description: Prior version of this requirement, if any. Proofs against the superseded CID remain valid statements; they are simply no longer about current law.

name.description: Machine name of the conjunct, matching its label in the elaborated term, e.g. 'efficiencyGap'.
